title: Community-based AI Governance
guidingQuestion: Who should decide how AI behaves in our communities?
summary: Communities shape AI behavior through participatory governance rather than accepting rules set only by vendors.

hero.headline: AI policy should not be a terms-of-service footnote.
hero.text: Model behavior affects classrooms, forums, and civic spaces. Community-based AI governance gives those spaces a real say in how assistance works among them.

problemStory.title: Why this matters
problemStory.scenario: A community forum enables an AI moderator tuned for engagement. Members wanted safety and nuance. They never got a vote; the vendor shipped a default.
stakes: One global default for plural contexts

webLimitations.title: Why today's Web struggles
webLimitations.text: AI governance is treated as a corporate risk function. Platforms lack durable mechanisms for communities to author, audit, and revise AI behavior in their contexts.

futureVision.title: Imagine instead
futureVision.text: Communities publish AI charters, review changes, and compose governance modules that travel with the group.
bullets: Transparent change logs communities can contest
